caption: AFTERMATH — Every failure should leave a safeguard. Recorded live from aftermath-7tij.vercel.app.
A claim is not evidence. When an agent says the work succeeded, AFTERMATH asks for the proof.
The investigation workspace is public: a visitor submits an incident with no credential.
Paste the incident. The material is parsed as data — never executed, never interpolated into a command.
Investigating: parse the evidence, form a hypothesis, propose a safeguard, then verify it against the decision engine.
The result is a Safeguard Record: evidence with verbatim spans, hypotheses with confidence, and a proposed safeguard.
Every link carries an honest state — observed, confirmed, unknown. A lookup that cannot run resolves to unknown, never to success.
Safeguard Records: every investigation, newest first — a connected chain from incident to memory.
The Memory Ledger reads live Walrus Memory Mainnet state from the relayer, namespace aftermath.
Completed and recall-verified writes are counted from durable records; simulated writes are excluded. The figures on screen are read live from this ledger.
The learning loop: investigate, learn, persist to Walrus Memory, recall during a later investigation, and change a decision.
Behaviour change is a real counterfactual: the same engine run with the recalled safeguard held out, then enforced.
Provenance closes the loop: the safeguard links back to the incident that produced it and every later investigation it reached.
Every failure should leave a safeguard.
